name: Reignition
genre: 1980s AOR / Melodic Stadium Rock / 80s Cosmic Pop
description: Ten years after exhaustion led the family to step away from the road on 2004's Progress Street ('Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street'), The Stardust Engine returns rested, recharged, and ready to perform again. Released in October 2015 immediately following Holly O'Connell's August 2015 Delaware Migration, Reignition ends the decade-long Burnout Hiatus with eleven brand-new 1980s AOR and cosmic synth-rock anthems.
subtitle: The 2015 Post-Hiatus Comeback Studio Album
linerNotes: At the end of 2004's Progress Street—and following the grueling 2003–2004 tour documented on 2005's Live in Norfolk—Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell closed 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street' with a solemn promise to Forger Nation: they were not breaking up, only turning the studio switches off until their bodies and minds had fully recharged from a decade of relentless recording and touring.

Aside from 2007's archival compilation Lost Sounds, 2008's intimate acoustic living-room session Our Own Frequency, and Cassidy's 2011 silver-anniversary studio re-imagining Starfield Calibration, the amplifiers on Progress Street NE remained quiet for a full decade. Then, in August 2015, CEO Holly O'Connell passed the Delaware Bar and executed 'The Delaware Migration'—folding Engine Room Records, LLC and the family's $2.4 billion portfolio into anonymous Delaware entities under The O'Connell Family Revocable Trust.

With the legal fortress permanently submerged and the five family members completely rested, Reignition is the sound of Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler walking back into their Blacksburg studio, lighting the main thrusters, and launching a brand-new chapter of 1980s melodic stadium rock and cosmic synth-pop.

studioArchives.title: Fulfilling the Promise of "Last Bus Home"
studioArchives.content: Where 2004's 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street' signed off for a decade of healing ('Lights out on Progress Street... Goodnight, Forger Nation'), the opening anthem 'Reignition: Lights Up on Progress Street' celebrates the morning the five siblings finally turned the studio amplifiers back on.

studioArchives.title: The Studio Prerequisite to Live at the Crucible (2016)
studioArchives.content: Because the family refused to return to the concert stage as a nostalgia act, Reignition had to come first—proving that thirty years after forming in a Blacksburg garage, The Stardust Engine's songwriting, sibling harmonies, and 1980s AOR/synth-rock fire burned brighter than ever.

studioArchives.title: August 2015: The Delaware Migration & The Norfolk Reckoning
studioArchives.content: Recorded during the summer and autumn of 2015—the same autumn Holly completed the Delaware Migration and CPI football avenged its 2014 38–0 Homecoming loss with a triumphant 52–0 shutout at VDU in Norfolk—Reignition captures a family and an alma mater in full flight.
